# Dot-com vs AI Bubble Comparison Dataset

## Overview
Four datasets capturing key market metrics across two technology-driven market booms: the 1997–2002 dot-com era and the 2021–2024 AI era. The data is structured for side-by-side temporal alignment using a common `quarter_offset` or `year` field within each era.

## Data Source

### nasdaq_index
Quarterly NASDAQ Composite closing values, rebased to 100 at the start of each era. Fields: `era` (string: "Dot-com" or "AI"), `quarter_offset` (integer 0–23), `label` (calendar quarter string), `index_value` (float). The dot-com series spans 24 quarters (1997-Q1 to 2002-Q4); the AI series spans 16 quarters (2021-Q1 to 2024-Q4).

### pe_ratio
Trailing 12-month P/E ratio for the NASDAQ Composite, sampled at irregular quarterly intervals. Fields: `era`, `quarter_offset`, `label`, `pe` (float, ratio). Dot-com P/E ranges from ~28 to ~105; AI-era P/E ranges from ~24 to ~40.

### ipo_counts
Annual count of technology-sector IPOs on US exchanges. Fields: `era`, `year` (integer), `ipo_count` (integer). Dot-com era: 6 years; AI era: 4 years.

### corporate_earnings
Aggregate annual net income for NASDAQ-100 companies in nominal billion USD. Fields: `era`, `year`, `earnings_bn` (float; may be negative). Dot-com earnings range from −12.3 to 30.5 B; AI-era earnings range from 358 to 510 B.

## Data Notes
- NASDAQ index values are rebased independently per era; absolute levels differ dramatically.
- P/E ratios for the dot-com era include periods of near-zero aggregate earnings, inflating the ratio.
- Nominal earnings are not inflation-adjusted; direct magnitude comparison across eras should note the ~20-year gap.
- 2024 figures are estimates based on analyst consensus as of late 2024.

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec
import numpy as np

with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

nasdaq = data['nasdaq_index']['data']
pe_ratio = data['pe_ratio']['data']
ipo_counts = data['ipo_counts']['data']
earnings = data['corporate_earnings']['data']

dotcom_nasdaq = [d for d in nasdaq if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_nasdaq = [d for d in nasdaq if d['era'] == 'AI']
dotcom_pe = [d for d in pe_ratio if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_pe = [d for d in pe_ratio if d['era'] == 'AI']
dotcom_ipo = [d for d in ipo_counts if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_ipo = [d for d in ipo_counts if d['era'] == 'AI']
dotcom_earn = [d for d in earnings if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_earn = [d for d in earnings if d['era'] == 'AI']

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')

gs = gridspec.GridSpec(2, 2, figure=fig, hspace=0.35, wspace=0.25)

colors = {'dotcom': '#B85450', 'ai': '#2E6B8A'}
accent_dotcom = '#D4766A'
accent_ai = '#4A9BBF'

ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])

# Panel 1: NASDAQ Index
ax1.set_facecolor('#FFFFFF')
q_dotcom = [d['quarter_offset'] for d in dotcom_nasdaq]
v_dotcom = [d['index_value'] for d in dotcom_nasdaq]
q_ai = [d['quarter_offset'] for d in ai_nasdaq]
v_ai = [d['index_value'] for d in ai_nasdaq]

ax1.plot(q_dotcom, v_dotcom, color=colors['dotcom'], linewidth=2, label='Dot-com (1997–2002)')
ax1.plot(q_ai, v_ai, color=colors['ai'], linewidth=2, label='AI (2021–2024)')

ax1.axvline(x=12, color=colors['ai'], linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, linewidth=1)
ax1.annotate('Peak', xy=(12, 305.2), xytext=(13, 290), fontsize=8, color=colors['dotcom'],
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['dotcom'], alpha=0.6))
ax1.annotate('AI High', xy=(15, 148.7), xytext=(13.5, 155), fontsize=8, color=colors['ai'],
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['ai'], alpha=0.6))
ax1.set_xlabel('Quarter Offset', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Index (base=100)', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('NASDAQ Composite Rebased to 100', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax1.set_xlim(-0.5, 24)
ax1.text(0.02, 0.98, 'Era Start → Era End', transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=8, va='top', alpha=0.6)

# Panel 2: P/E Ratio
ax2.set_facecolor('#FFFFFF')
q_dpe = [d['quarter_offset'] for d in dotcom_pe]
v_dpe = [d['pe'] for d in dotcom_pe]
q_ape = [d['quarter_offset'] for d in ai_pe]
v_ape = [d['pe'] for d in ai_pe]

ax2.bar([x + 0.2 for x in q_ape], v_ape, width=0.4, color=colors['ai'], alpha=0.85, label='AI')
ax2.axhline(y=100, color='#999', linestyle=':', alpha=0.6, linewidth=1)
ax2.annotate('Dot-com Peak: 105.2×', xy=(12, 105.2), xytext=(8, 112), fontsize=8, color=colors['dotcom'],

ax2.annotate('AI Recent: 40.3×', xy=(15, 40.3), xytext=(11, 45), fontsize=8, color=colors['ai'],
             arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['ai'], alpha=0.6))
ax2.set_xlabel('Quarter Offset', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('P/E Ratio (×)', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Price-to-Earnings Ratio Comparison', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')
ax2.set_xlim(-1, 25)

# Panel 3: IPO Counts
ax3.set_facecolor('#FFFFFF')
years_d = [d['year'] for d in dotcom_ipo]
counts_d = [d['ipo_count'] for d in dotcom_ipo]
years_a = [d['year'] for d in ai_ipo]
counts_a = [d['ipo_count'] for d in ai_ipo]

x_d = np.arange(len(years_d))
x_a = np.arange(len(years_a))
width = 0.35
bars1 = ax3.bar(x_d - width/2, counts_d, width, color=colors['dotcom'], alpha=0.85, label='Dot-com')
bars2 = ax3.bar(x_a + width/2, counts_a, width, color=colors['ai'], alpha=0.85, label='AI')
ax3.set_xticks(np.arange(max(len(years_d), len(years_a))))
ax3.set_xticklabels(list(range(1997, 2003)), fontsize=9)
ax3.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_ylabel('IPO Count', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_title('Technology IPO Volume by Year', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=9)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

ax4.set_facecolor('#FFFFFF')
ax4.fill_between([d['year'] for d in dotcom_earn], [d['earnings_bn'] for d in dotcom_earn],
                 color=colors['dotcom'], alpha=0.3)
ax4.plot([d['year'] for d in dotcom_earn], [d['earnings_bn'] for d in dotcom_earn],
         color=colors['dotcom'], linewidth=2, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Dot-com')

                 color=colors['ai'], alpha=0.3)
ax4.plot([d['year'] for d in ai_earn], [d['earnings_bn'] for d in ai_earn],
         color=colors['ai'], linewidth=2, marker='s', markersize=5, label='AI')
ax4.axhline(y=0, color='#666', linestyle='-', linewidth=0.8)
ax4.annotate('2001 Loss: −$12.3B', xy=(2001, -12.3), xytext=(1999.5, -30), fontsize=8,
             color=colors['dotcom'], ha='center', arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['dotcom'], alpha=0.6))
ax4.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylabel('Earnings (Billion USD)', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('NASDAQ-100 Aggregate Corporate Earnings', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left', fontsize=9)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax4.set_xlim(1996.5, 2002.5)
ax5 = ax4.twiny()
ax5.set_xlim(ax4.get_xlim())
ax5.set_xticks([2021, 2022, 2023, 2024])
ax5.set_xticklabels(['2021', '2022', '2023', '2024'], fontsize=8)
ax5.tick_params(axis='x', length=0)
ax4.text(0.98, 0.02, 'AI Era Data →', transform=ax4.transAxes, fontsize=8, va='bottom', ha='right', alpha=0.7)

fig.suptitle('Dot-com vs. AI Era: A Comparative Market Analysis', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
plt.close()
print("Chart saved successfully")
